chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: Chicago tuba players: Singleton Palmer, Buddy Gross, Beauford
summary: Many Chicago tuba players took solos.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Twelve-year term, huh? I heard -- you may know him, a tuba player from St. Louis. I worked a gig with him a couple years ago, just a one-nighter. Had a band -- Singleton Palmer.
Who plays the thing like a trombone. Had you known him before?
Yeah, I knew him years ago, yeah.
He played string bass with Ba sie, oh, much later, I think, in the late forties, or something like that, when Walter Paige had left. So I was really surprised the way he played tuba.
Oh, yeah, man, he's a fine tuba player.

Who are some of the other tuba players around town here? That particularly impressed you. Who was the fellow who recorded with Louie -- can't think of his name, now. Cyril something? Not St. Cyr -- my mind's blank.
Well, who were some of the other tuba players around Chicago?
Well, there's one I had in mind, was -- what the heck was his name? Buddy Gross.

Yeah, that was one. And...(another) he made some records in my place with Jelly Roll -- Beauford. Beauford, he was one of the great solo tuba players around Chicago. We had several. In fact, most of the tuba players around Chicago could play solos.
What were some of the solos that they played?
On anything. Just take a chorus or two.
